=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer-Side Review of Seller's SPA Positions and Disclosure Letter

**Bottom line:** The package is heavily seller-favourable. It would leave Wattlebridge carrying most of the known risks, which total roughly AUD 4.2m before the unquantified privacy and Bluefen exposures. The "FINAL / not to be re-opened" framing and the "market context" paragraph are negotiating positions, not binding terms. Wattlebridge should not accept them without confirming what its principals have actually approved, and should check whether any term sheet or exclusivity letter creates an obligation.

## 1. Liability, thresholds and limitation structure

**Cap (12.1): 20% of price (AUD 4.8m).** This is at the top of the range the Seller itself cites, and it is the same cap for everything. Push for a general cap of around 30%, with fundamental warranties, tax and specific indemnities carved out.

**Thresholds (12.2): AUD 25k de minimis and AUD 250k deductible basket (about 1.04% of price).** The basket is a deductible: only the excess is recoverable. Illustration: if the known items (Ironquay AUD 180k, bonuses AUD 420k, supplier renewals AUD 330k) were warranty claims, the basket alone would absorb about AUD 250k of them. Push for:
- a tipping basket (once exceeded, recovery is from the first dollar), set at around 0.5% of price;
- a de minimis of AUD 5k–10k;
- exclusion of specific indemnities from both thresholds.

**Time limits (12.3/13): 18 months for general claims, applied to all claims.** This would cut off claims that often surface only after the first audit or tax cycle, and would also shorten the periods for fundamental and tax claims. Push for:
- general warranties: 24–36 months;
- title, capacity and fundamental warranties: 6 years (the usual NSW contract limitation period is 6 years, so the Seller's 18 months is a material shortening; confirm with NSW counsel);
- tax: the statutory period plus a buffer (e.g., 60 days after the ATO period closes), or at least 6 years;
- specific indemnities (privacy, IP, Bluefen, Riverlark): until fully resolved or 6 years, whichever is later.

**Fundamental/title under general caps (proposal).** Reject. Title and capacity warranties should be capped at the full price and survive 6 years.

## 2. Exclusivity, non-reliance and buyer knowledge

**Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applying to "all Claims of any nature" (9.3/12.8/20.5).** This would catch fraud. Push for an express carve-out for fraud and wilful misconduct. Non-reliance clauses also need checking against Australian Consumer Law misleading-conduct protections; Australian counsel should confirm what can be excluded.

**Data room and public record disclosure (1.1, 1.2, Schedule 7).** A blanket disclosure of the entire data room and public registers would qualify every warranty against everything in the data room, which is effectively a wholesale waiver. Reject. Require:
- specific disclosure against specific warranties, with a fair-disclosure standard;
- no general data room disclosure;
- disclosure that cannot qualify specific indemnities.

**Buyer knowledge bar (8.3).** This is an anti-sandbagging clause. The Seller would use it to defeat claims on the very issues it has disclosed. Under Australian law, the effect of buyer knowledge on warranty claims is not settled, so the contract should be explicit. Delete 8.3 and insert an express pro-sandbagging clause: the Buyer's knowledge does not prejudice its rights, particularly for matters addressed by specific indemnities.

## 3. Specific issues

**Bluefen (about AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue, about 30%).** Consent is not in hand and conditions in 11.3 are unsatisfied. The Seller's proposal is "reasonable endeavours" and deemed satisfaction on delivery of a written consent that may still carry conditions. Push for:
- written, unconditional Bluefen consent as a condition precedent, with Wattlebridge's right to walk away if it is not obtained;
- confirmation that the consent covers the 11.3 conditions, or evidence that they are satisfied;
- a price adjustment or escrow if the consent is conditional.

**Riverlark (about AUD 3.2m outstanding).** Discharge "following Completion" is not acceptable under a debt-free, cash-free deal. Push for:
- a payout letter and discharge of security delivered at Completion;
- the payout deducted from the price in the funds flow;
- a PPSR search confirming release.

**Ironquay IP (AUD 180k open; DD-004 clause 7.3).** Transfer of SOW3 Project Materials is conditional on payment of every SOW3 fee, and none is evidenced. The Seller's indemnity limited to SOW3 payment is inadequate. Push for:
- evidence of payment, or payment by the Seller before Completion;
- a confirmatory assignment of Project Materials as a condition precedent;
- a specific indemnity for IP ownership and any unpaid fees, outside the cap and basket;
- an IP ownership warranty.

**Employee bonuses (AUD 420k, DD-005).** These are excluded from the funds flow, and their on-costs are not addressed. Transaction-related bonuses are debt-like. Push for:
- treatment as indebtedness deducted from price, or paid by the Seller;
- inclusion of payroll tax and superannuation (super is currently 12%; NSW payroll tax may apply). Indicatively, on-costs could be roughly AUD 50k–75k, to be verified.

**Privacy/export incident (DD-006; about 1,240 records with names, business emails, roles, timestamps).** The Seller's "not expected to be material" is unsupported. The data set is personal information, and the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) notifiable data breaches regime may apply if an eligible data breach has occurred or is likely. Push for:
- a forensic investigation before signing, or a specific indemnity pending its outcome;
- a specific, uncapped (or separately capped) indemnity covering notification, regulatory, remediation and third-party costs;
- Buyer control of notification and regulator dealings post-Completion;
- a 6-year survival period.

**Office lease (DD-007).** The notification obligation may require landlord consent or an estoppel. Push for landlord consent or estoppel as a condition precedent if the lease requires it, and a specific indemnity for any lease consequences.

**Supplier renewals (AUD 330k aggregate; DD-008/011).** The Seller calls these ordinary course. Three near-simultaneous renewals of AUD 110k each look like commitments that may extend beyond Completion. Push for:
- full contract terms and termination rights;
- treatment of unavoidable or accrued amounts as debt-like;
- a conduct of business covenant requiring Buyer consent to new or renewed commitments before Completion.

**Mossvale (DD-009).** The assignment restriction does not on its face require consent to a share sale. Push for written confirmation from Mossvale, or a consent condition precedent, if the restriction is drafted as change of control.

**Title (DD-012).** The share register shows Harbourglass as 100% holder, but that is not verification. Before signing:
- obtain an ASIC current company extract;
- inspect the original register and check for transfer restrictions or pre-emption rights in the constitution;
- run a PPSR search for encumbrances over the shares;
- obtain a Seller title warranty and a statutory declaration.

## 4. Summary of recommendations

**Structure**
1. Reject the "FINAL / not to be re-opened" framing. Confirm what Wattlebridge's principals approved and whether any binding term sheet or exclusivity letter exists.
2. Replace the blanket data room disclosure with specific disclosure and a fair-disclosure standard.
3. Delete the buyer-knowledge bar and insert an express pro-sandbagging clause.
4. Carve out fraud from the exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions.

**Financial protection**
5. General cap: open around 30%, fallback 20–25%.
6. Fundamental, title and capacity warranties: full price cap, 6-year survival.
7. Tax: statutory period plus buffer, outside the general cap.
8. Tipping basket around 0.5% of price; de minimis AUD 5k–10k; thresholds not applying to specific indemnities.
9. General warranties: 24–36 months.
10. Consider an escrow or retention to support claims. The amount is a commercial decision; a range of about 10% of price (AUD 2.4m) for 18–24 months is a reasonable starting point for discussion.

**Specific indemnities** (outside caps, baskets and general disclosure)
11. Bluefen consent and any conditions.
12. Riverlark debt and security.
13. Ironquay SOW3 fees and IP ownership.
14. Employee bonuses and on-costs.
15. Privacy/export incident.
16. Lease, supplier renewals, and Mossvale.

**Conditions and funds flow**
17. Bluefen unconditional consent as a condition precedent, with a walk-away right.
18. Riverlark payout letter and discharge delivered at Completion, deducted from price.
19. Bonuses, on-costs and any unpaid Ironquay fees treated as debt-like in the funds flow.
20. Landlord and Mossvale consents or confirmations as conditions precedent, where required.
21. Forensic findings on the privacy incident before signing.

**Interim period**
22. Conduct of business covenant: no new or renewed supplier commitments, bonus changes or privacy-related steps without Buyer consent.

**Verification**
23. ASIC extract, register inspection, constitution review, PPSR search, and title warranty and statutory declaration.

**Caveats:** This review is based on the Seller's summary and disclosure letter, not the full SPA. Clause references are the Seller's own. The NSW limitation period, Privacy Act, payroll tax, superannuation, and Australian Consumer Law points should be confirmed by Australian counsel before they are relied on in negotiation.
